content:
Apple TV has long been called "the new HBO" because it prioritises quality over quantity. But in recent months, the streaming service's watchlist has been piling up and I can't keep up at all.

Apple TV steps into a new era as quality and quantity rise together

I have been subscribed since Apple TV first launched in 2019, and at any given time the platform usually only has one or two shows I want to watch.

This output model resembles HBO, which built its brand on producing a small number of generally high-quality series.

Over the past few years, however, Apple's output has gradually increased, and at the same time the hit rate of its titles also seems to have improved.

The result is that Apple now simply has too many great shows for me to watch them all.

The following are Apple TV's new series airing each week right now:

  • Ted Lasso — one of my all-time favourite shows
  • Slow Horses — another of Apple's best series ever
  • Dark Matter — a sci-fi series I was completely hooked on during season one, though I haven't started season two yet
  • Brothers — a brand-new half-hour comedy starring Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson that looks pretty fun
  • Last Seen — a new thriller with solid reviews that I haven't watched yet
  • There's also Women in Blue and Knife Edge, which I might catch during a slow period, but for now they're further down the queue

I'm really looking forward to catching up on Dark Matter season two, because season one already put it among my favourite sci-fi shows, second only to Severance and Pluribus. I just haven't been able to find the time to start it. Half-hour comedies are always my go-to for something light, so Brothers has already made it onto the watchlist.

I like crime thrillers and shows centred on families, so Last Seen is right up my alley, but even with a Stephen King endorsement I still haven't started it.

And the above is only what is currently airing.

I haven't caught up with Silo season three, and I haven't started Sugar season two either, even though the latter has great reviews and I'm a fan. If I dropped all the other streaming services, I could watch Apple TV's catalogue non-stop, but the other platforms' offerings are keeping me just as busy.

October is almost here, and Apple has as many as seven brand-new series and films premiering — the most I can remember in a single month.

In short, I'm genuinely glad that Apple TV is doing so well now. It beat HBO at the Emmys this year, and there's good reason for it.

What do you think of Apple TV's current and recent slate? Feel free to share your thoughts in the comments.

Apple TV costs US$14.99 per month, or it can be subscribed as part of an Apple One bundle.
